title: How ESP Works(?)
summary: Josh and Chuck open in their new studio, then examine ESP (extrasensory perception): its categories (telepathy, clairvoyance, precognition, retrocognition, mediumship, psychometry, telekinesis), the origin of the term and the coinage of "psi" by a 1940s researcher, the early Society for Psychical Research and fraud exposure (Madame Blavatsky), J.B. Rhine's Duke University card experiments with Zener cards and sensory leakage controls, Princeton's PEAR random number generator studies, the Titan/Titanic novella coincidence, the fMRI study, spillover/other-dimension theories, Daryl Bem's precognition experiments and the criticism of them, cold reading and James Randi, and the CIA remote viewing program. Ends with a listener mail on pronouncing plant family names.

entities.name: The Men Who Stare at Goats

segments.title: New studio and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck (with Jerry) welcome listeners to their new studio, joke about its size and setup, and introduce the topic of ESP, with Chuck saying he doesn't believe in it and Josh saying he keeps an open mind.

segments.title: ESP definition and categories
segments.summary: ESP is an umbrella term coined by J.B. Rhine, and 'psi' was later coined in the 1940s as a less supernatural-sounding alternative. The hosts list categories: telepathy, clairvoyance, precognition, retrocognition (including the spotted-dog example), mediumship, psychometry and telekinesis.

segments.title: Early psychical research and frauds
segments.summary: Discussion of the Society for Psychical Research and William James, who exposed fraudulent mediums such as Madame Blavatsky while investigating unexplained cases with an open mind. Also a digression on Blavatsky and the Source Family documentary.

segments.title: Scientific ESP theories and the fMRI study
segments.summary: Describes the electromagnetic-spectrum explanation, which fell out of favor because signal strength would weaken with distance, unlike ESP results. Covers an MRI study finding no brain region reacting differently to ESP stimuli, and the spillover-from-another-dimension idea.

segments.title: Titan novella and Titanic coincidence
segments.summary: Morgan Robertson's 1898 novella Futility, about the ship Titan striking an iceberg, is compared with the Titanic sinking fourteen years later. The hosts explain the similarities and how the story embellished over time, such as the claim it came in a trance.

segments.title: J.B. Rhine and Zener card experiments
segments.summary: Rhine's 1930s experiments at Duke with Zener cards, including a sample online test Chuck took, and the statistical discussion of chance. Also covers Hubert Pierce's results, translucent early cards, and Rhine's controls for sensory leakage with the Ganzfeld setup.

segments.title: Princeton PEAR random number generator studies
segments.summary: Princeton's Engineering Anomalies Research lab ran decades of random number generator trials, finding a very slight but measurable human-thought effect on the output. Also discusses how machine experiments bear on telepathy versus clairvoyance.

segments.title: Criticism of Rhine and the Levy affair
segments.summary: Rhine's critics note he excluded results from subjects he suspected of cheating and that he was a believer. The Levy affair is described, in which an engineer unplugged the censor to record only positive hits; Rhine fired him. Rhine is still considered a researcher under close scrutiny.

segments.title: Daryl Bem's precognition experiments
segments.summary: Cornell psychologist Daryl Bem's experiments, including the erotic image test with a 53.1 percent hit rate, the reverse-priming word recall test, and the criticism and failed reproducibility that followed. The hosts compare effect size to aspirin and heart attack prevention.

segments.title: Cold reading, James Randi and CIA remote viewing
segments.summary: Cold reading by stage psychics like John Edward is contrasted with the research debate. James Randi's one-million-dollar challenge is mentioned, and the hosts discuss the declassified CIA ESP program and a Nightline segment with Ted Koppel and Robert Gates.

segments.title: Sponsor and carpenter shout-out
segments.summary: Josh gives a shout-out to a listener's carpentry business in Kansas and the nonprofit Outreach Program.

segments.title: Listener mail: pronouncing plant family names
segments.summary: A botanist listener, Jane, explains that plant family names end in -aceae, pronounced by spelling out the final letters, using the example of Anacardiaceae for poison oak.
